test_title: PYST 36: RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I - Mathematics (Held On: 28 Aug, 2025 Shift 3)
subject: maths
question: 8 years ago, the age of a father was 20 years more than twice his son's age. After how many years, from now, will he be twice his son's age?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Let F and S be the ages of the father and son. We will track the expression (F − 2S) over time.

8 years ago, F − 2S = 20.

Every year, both F and S increase by 1, so the expression (F − 2S) decreases by exactly 1 every year.

Current value of (F − 2S) at present = 20 − 8 = 12.

For the father to be exactly twice his son's age, the value of (F − 2S) must become 0.

The time required to reduce from 12 to 0 at a rate of 1 per year is exactly 12 years.

**∴ The correct answer is 12 years.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Let the present age of the father be F years and the son be S years.

8 years ago, Father's age = (F − 8) years and Son's age = (S − 8) years.

 
• 
 
 
 8 Years Ago
 F − 8 = 2(S − 8) + 20
 
 
 Present
 F, S
 
 
 After x Years
 F + x = 2(S + x)
 
 

 + 8 years
 
 

 + x years

**Calculations:**

⇒ F − 8 = 2 × (S − 8) + 20

⇒ F − 8 = 2S − 16 + 20

⇒ F − 8 = 2S + 4

⇒ F − 2S = 12 --- (Equation 1)

Let after x years, the father's age be twice the son's age.

⇒ F + x = 2 × (S + x)

⇒ F + x = 2S + 2x

⇒ x = F − 2S

Substituting the value of (F − 2S) from Equation 1 into the above expression:

⇒ x = 12

**∴ The correct answer is 12 years.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Constant Age Difference

The absolute difference between the ages of two individuals is constant at any point in time, past or future. If person A is older than B by 5 years today, they will always be 5 years older.

Convergence of Age Ratios

As both individuals grow older by the exact same amount each year, the ratio of their ages continuously moves closer to 1:1 further into the future.

Present Age Variable Setup

For simple formulation, always assume present ages as variables like x and y. Then, t years ago ages are (x − t) and (y − t), and t years later they are (x + t) and (y + t).

Tracking Age Multipliers

If finding when one age will be k times the other, tracking the expression (A − k × B) is faster. Since both ages increase by 1 per year, the expression changes by (1 − k) each year.
